children: BACK TO THE POST-SUMMER GRIND: STOCKS END RED

Wall Street lost some ground on Tuesday as investors returned from their three-day holiday weekend only to be confronted by an expanding Middle East conflict, retaliatory tariffs from Canada and crude prices touching a six-week high.
While the Nasdaq
and the S&P 500
ended the day only modestly lower, the blue-chip Dow
suffered the steepest loss, weighed down by drugmaker Amgen
, following Novartis'
disappointing cholesterol drug study and BMO's downgrade of the stock.
Utilities
were among the top performers among the S&P 500's 11 major sectors, benefiting from a U.S. heatwave, while energy stocks
got a boost from rising crude. Amgen helped drag healthcare
to the sharpest percentage decline.

Hostilities in the Middle East ramped up, following attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on four Saudi cities and Israel's decision to shutter the British consulate in East Jerusalem after the UK, France and Canada banned imports from Israeli settlements in the West Bank.
Closer to home, Canada's counter-tariffs, on $20 billion worth of U.S. goods, took effect at midnight, and covered everything from steel to furniture to clothing and electronics.
Elsewhere in the market, chips
had a good day, with Intel
, AMD
, and Seagate Technology
rising between 5.9% and 9.1%. Nvidia
, on the other hand, lost 2.0%.
On the losing end, travel & leisure stocks (.SPCOMHOTL), and housing-related shares
, (.SPCOMHOME) were obvious underperformers, dropping between 2.8% and 3.8%.

On the economics front, small business sentiment dipped as expectations of near-term business conditions deteriorated. Later in the week, the Labor Department's Producer Price and Consumer Price indexes are expected on Thursday and Friday, respectively.

These two inflation indicators could move the expectations needle regarding the Fed's September rate decision. Financial markets are currently baking in a 60.4% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike when the central bank convenes next week.
Here's your closing snapshot:
US stock indexes fall: Nasdaq ends down ~0.3%, S&P 500 off ~0.6%, Dow down ~1.2%
Healthcare weakest S&P 500 sector; energy leads gainers
Dollar ~flat; gold, bitcoin both down ~1%; US crude up ~2.8%
US 10-year Treasury yield edges up to ~4.79%
